h1: The Sarojin — a quiet adults-only resort on White Sand Beach, Khao Lak
intro: Khao Lak is a far quieter coast than Phuket or Krabi — made for travellers who want to escape the crowds and actually fall asleep to the waves. The Sarojin is a Luxury, adults-only resort right on White Sand Beach that many rate as the best stay in the area. With no children under 10, it's exceptionally peaceful: 56 residences set in lush gardens around an ancient ficus tree, an infinity pool, Pathways Spa, and the beachfront Edge restaurant. From approx. THB 6,500/night. Scored 9.6 from 52 Trip.com reviews.

body.html: The Sarojin has been open since 2005 and has stayed one of the most talked-about resorts in Khao Lak ever since. What sets it apart from the bigger resorts is that it's adults-only — no children under 10. The result is a calm that's genuinely hard to find: no kids running into the pool, no loud family activities. The whole resort holds just 56 residences, laid out across lush gardens around the ancient ficus tree that has become its signature.

Rooms start with the Garden Residence at 95 sqm — several times larger than the standard room at most 5-star resorts. Every residence has a King bed, an open-air lounge pavilion or balcony, a generous bathroom, and clean, contemporary Asian decor that's elegant without clutter. Step up and you get the Pool Residence (120 sqm with a private pool), the Jacuzzi Pool Suite (150 sqm), or the Two-Bedroom Pool Residence (215 sqm) for groups or couples who want extra space. Guests regularly praise how clean and well-maintained the rooms are, right down to the details.
"We woke up, had coffee in our garden pavilion, heard only the waves and the birds, and walked a few steps to the white-sand beach — so quiet it felt like we had the whole resort to ourselves."

The heart of the place is its setting on White Sand Beach in Khuk Khak — wide, quiet, and a few minutes' walk from your room. There's an infinity pool in the garden, the well-regarded Pathways Spa, and a fitness centre. Dining is a real strength: Edge sits right on the beachfront for Thai and international food with a sea view, while Ficus tucks under the canopy of the old ficus tree beside the lotus pond for Mediterranean cuisine. The thing guests mention most is the à la carte breakfast you can order any time from early morning to evening — every dish cooked fresh, not a self-serve buffet.

The honest trade-off with The Sarojin is its distance from the airport and town. Khao Lak is about 1 to 1.5 hours by car from Phuket Airport (HKT). The area is peaceful, but that means restaurants and shops outside the resort are limited, so getting out requires a car. And because it's adults-only, families with young children simply can't stay. It scores 9.6 from 52 Trip.com reviews and 4.8/5 from over 2,400 TripAdvisor reviews (ranked #2 in Khuk Khak) — numbers few would argue with.

The Sarojin isn't for everyone. If you're travelling as a family with kids, or you want a large resort with lots of activities and several restaurants, this isn't it. But if this trip is about quiet, privacy, and service that genuinely cares — for couples, honeymooners, or anyone set on a slow-life seaside rest — The Sarojin delivers that in a way few resorts in Khao Lak can match. Rates start from approx. THB 6,500/night for a Garden Residence in low season, climbing to THB 11,000+ in high season.

A tip from reading the reviews: if the budget stretches, upgrade to a Pool Residence for a private pool in the garden — it pays off especially with the adults-only calm. Don't miss booking a treatment at Pathways Spa ahead of time, and try dinner at the beachfront Edge at sunset. In high season (November–April), the best rooms go fast, so book 1–2 months ahead.

But accept that it's adults-only (families with young kids can't stay), it's a way from the airport and town, and the price isn't for every trip.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — The Sarojin, Khao Lak, Phang Nga

faq.q: Where is The Sarojin and how do I get there?
faq.a: The Sarojin sits right on White Sand Beach in Khuk Khak, Khao Lak, Phang Nga Province. It's about 1–1.5 hours by car from Phuket Airport (HKT), and around 10 minutes from Pakarang Cape and Bang Niang Beach. The resort can arrange an airport transfer — request it when you book.

faq.q: How much does The Sarojin cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 6,500/night for a Garden Residence (95 sqm). From there you can step up to a Pool Residence (120 sqm with a private pool), a Jacuzzi Pool Suite (150 sqm), and a Two-Bedroom Pool Residence (215 sqm). High-season rates climb to THB 11,000+, so compare a few platforms before booking.

The Sarojin is an adults-only resort and does not accept children under 10. That's why it's so quiet and private — ideal for couples, honeymooners, or anyone after a genuine rest. Families with young children should choose a family-friendly resort instead, such as JW Marriott Khao Lak.

faq.q: Who is The Sarojin best for?
faq.a: It suits couples, honeymooners, or anyone set on a slow-life seaside rest. The adults-only setting is quiet and the service is attentive. It's for travellers who want privacy and calm, not a large resort with lots of activities.

faq.q: What is the food like at The Sarojin?
faq.a: There are two restaurants — Edge, on the beachfront, serving Thai and international food with a sea view, and Ficus, under the old ficus tree beside the lotus pond, serving Mediterranean cuisine. The most-praised feature is the à la carte breakfast you can order any time from morning to evening, cooked fresh, alongside a wine bar and wine cellar.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and can I cancel?
faq.a: In high season (November–April), book 1–2 months ahead as there are only 56 residences. Other times, 3–4 weeks is usually fine. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — pick that first if your plans aren't firm, then compare prices across a few sites before confirming.
